title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: slab position of billed demurrage days
content:
## Scope

This rule of the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category decides which charge slab each billed demurrage day of a per-container record falls in, and it sets the order in which the two final lines of a combined-clock record are booked.

## Booking order on a combined clock

> When demurrage and detention run on one merged clock, the record's detention row is booked before its demurrage row.

Put in desk terms: on a record whose clock model is combined, the final detention line is booked before the final demurrage line.

## Slab count

1. Under the separate clock model, the slab count of the demurrage days starts at the first demurrage day.
2. Under the combined clock model, on an export record the slab count of the demurrage days continues after the chargeable days of the detention line already booked on the record, counting none when the record carries no detention line.
3. Under the combined clock model, on an import record the slab count starts at the first chargeable day.
4. The slab of a demurrage day follows its position in that count: slab 1 up to the slab 1 length, slab 2 up to the slab 1 and slab 2 lengths together, slab 3 up to the three lengths together, and slab 4 for any later position.

## Input, judgement, output

> **Input**: the clock model, the direction, the billed demurrage days, and, on a combined export record, the chargeable days of the detention line booked on the record.
> **Judgement**: where does the count of the demurrage days begin?
> **Output**: on a combined export record the first demurrage day takes the position after the booked detention days; otherwise it takes position 1.

## Worked example (hypothetical slab lengths of 4, 4 and 8 days, used only to show the counting)

A combined export record whose booked detention line carries 5 chargeable days bills 6 demurrage days. They take slab positions 6 to 11: positions 6, 7 and 8 are slab 2 days and positions 9, 10 and 11 are slab 3 days.

| Situation | Slab 1 | Slab 2 | Slab 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Detention line with 5 chargeable days already booked | 0 | 3 | 3 |
| No detention line on the record (count starts at position 1) | 4 | 2 | 0 |

The two rows give different demurrage amounts, which is why the booked detention line matters to the count. On a record under the separate clock model, or on a combined import record, the slab count of the demurrage days does not draw on the booked detention line, so booking the detention line leaves those demurrage days in the slabs they already fall in.
